title: Individual Placement and Support Programme - AWARD
description:
Norfolk County Council has been awarded grant funding by the Department for Work and Pensions and Department for Health & Social Care (DHSC) to participate in the Individual Placement and Support in Primary Care initiative. The project is called Working Well Norfolk (WW - Norfolk) and the aim of WW - Norfolk is to support people with disabilities in to, and to stay in, work. 
      
      This contract is for an Activity Delivery Partner (ADP) to deliver WW - Norfolk across the county, in accordance with the funding terms set out by the DWP. This will enable the continued growth of the Individual Placement Support (IPS) model of supported employment services.
      
      Norfolk County Council (NCC) has procured a lead provider to deliver the WW - Norfolk service for Norfolk residents. The service, funded by the Department for Work & Pensions (DWP), will provide support for 1100 Norfolk residents between 1 October 2023 and 31 March 2025. The contract was let on a fixed budget, and as such price was not evaluated in this procurement.
      
      The WW - Norfolk service will sit within the NCC Growth and Development suite of programmes and delivery and is expected to take place in co-locations within a range of primary and community NHS health services and professionals. 
      
      Participants will come from two distinct cohorts:
      o Out of work participants who require assistance and support to move into competitive employment; and
      o In work participants who are off sick or struggling in the workplace due to their disability / health condition.

title: Active Norfolk Activity Finder
description:
Active Norfolk is seeking to appoint a contractor to design and build a bespoke peer-to-peer web directory to connect Norfolk residents with physical activity opportunities in a user-friendly way.
Active Norfolk is one of over 40 Active Partnerships covering England. The organisation aims to increase participation in sport and physical activity for Norfolk residents. We do this by providing information about local opportunities for individuals to get active, and provide support for clubs, volunteers and coaches.
It has become clear that in order to facilitate this role effectively and deliver the most effective project outcomes, an effective and relevant database of active opportunities within Norfolk will be an
invaluable tool. 
The development of this initiative is in conjunction with several different projects coordinated by Norfolk County Council, including the MONUMENT project, which aims to provide active opportunities to carers of people living with dementia. As
well as the Experience Project, which aims to boost experiential out-of-season tourism in Norfolk. The Activity Finder development will play a major role in achieving the desired outcomes for both projects.
Purpose of the Activity Finder: 
The purpose of the activity finder site is to act as a hub for all active opportunities of all types across Norfolk. It will enable Norfolk residents to find ways to be
active which suit them. This includes exercise classes, gyms and sports centres, green spaces, cycle trails and much more. The platform must be built in such a way that flexibility is a priority as activities is such a broad sector. 
The beneficiaries of the activity finder are wide-ranging, including the general public who will benefit from an accurate and informative database of exercise
opportunities. Partnering organisations which Active Norfolk works with to deliver specific projects. As well as healthcare providers and social prescribers who will be able to use a trusted database with reviews, filters and kitemarking to recommend specific activities to
patients.

title: Reducing Hopelessness Through Positive Activities   - AWARD
description:
Norfolk County Council has procure a service which is aimed at supporting men in Norfolk aged 18 and above presenting to GPs feeling depressed and hopeless. The procurement will be delivering against Public Health and the National strategy for Suicide Prevention priorities with agreed targets and deliverables. Our overarching aim is to reduce deaths by suicide in Norfolk to as close to zero as possible.  
      
      Over 75% of those who take their own lives are male. Men often do not feel comfortable in seeking advice or support from traditional services available and some fall back on coping strategies that may be damaging to their health e.g., alcohol and drugs.  The delivery partner will deliver the prevention and positive activities (PPA) work across Norfolk & Waveney. They will deliver this through a strengths-based approach supporting men to promote positive mental health outcomes by developing a better understanding of themselves throughout the various life stages. The work will be a mix of direct delivery, group work and partnership working, supporting men to engage with other services where necessary. The service will be committed to supporting men to overcome persistent and enduring challenges using approaches and techniques that will help them make the positive change needed in their wellbeing.
      
      The contract will be a multi-year opportunity working in close partnership with the Local Authority delivering to men across Norfolk.

title: Greater Norwich NSSA -New Settlement Master Planning - Town Planning and Landscape - AWARD
description:
Greater Norwich, comprising the local authorities of South Norfolk Council (SNC), Broadland District Council (BDC) and Norwich City Council (NCC), also working with Norfolk County Council (Norfolk CC), has an established track record of partnership working in the context of plan-making, strategic infrastructure planning and investment.   
      The potential for delivery of a new settlement, or settlements, in the Greater Norwich area was considered during the preparation of the, now adopted, Greater Norwich Local Plan (GNLP).   Whilst none of the potential new settlement sites considered were allocated, the adopted GNLP identified that any review of the local plan in the future would assess the potential for a new settlement or settlements.   
      In the context of a proposed GNLP Review, the Greater Norwich Development Partnership (GNDP) has recently committed to developing an evidence base and exploring the potential allocation of land for a new settlement or settlements. It is also likely, ahead of a likely devolution process, that Norfolk and Suffolk will be embarking on the creation of a strategic Spatial Development Strategy (SDS) so there is a further imperative to consider strategic growth opportunities for Greater Norwich, positioned within a wider context. 
      This consultancy appointment is being jointly commissioned by SNC and BDC, on behalf of the GNDP. 
      A Call for Sites has been undertaken (Spring '26) in preparation for the GNLP Review - with the new plan being prepared in accordance with the new plan-making system - and three potential new settlement sites have been promoted. These are the same sites promoted through the last plan-making process. 
      The purpose of this commission is to procure a consultant to provide strategic Master planning and Landscape advice to support in 'triaging' three potential new settlement sites to inform the Site Assessment process and the identification of preferred new settlement site(s) prior to the proposed Regulation 23 Consultation.

It is therefore NCC's intention to appoint a contractor from the start of RIBA stage 2 under a 2 stage D&B contract, as the project will have significant MMC elements and the design contractor needs to engage in design much earlier than in a standard 2-stage D&B. Appointing the main contractor in this manner will result in there not being a typical client-side design team and would produce performance specifications up to end of RIBA stage 3. The client therefore retains a small team from each of the companies, responsible for the RIBA stage 1 report, as technical guardians. The purpose of the design guardians, is to check and ensure the integrity of the stage 1 report and its intentions around sustainability is not compromised. This will not exclude the companies from partnering with contractors bidding for the works. A clerk of works will also be appointed client side. The budget for the construction element of this project is £8,734,000 inclusive of construction prelims, overheads, and profits. Norfolk County Council wishes to engage with building contractors prior to issue of a contract notice. If you wish to engage with us, please express an interest in this project and use the correspondence facility. We anticipate that any planned pre-tender contractor engagement meeting will be conducted over Teams during early February 2023.

title: Healthy Lifestyles Framework Agreement - AWARD
description:
Norfolk County Council's Public Health department have created a Light Touch Regime Framework Agreement for providers of services supporting Healthy Lifestyles.
      
      At the outset of this Framework Agreement the public health team are purchasing Structured Support Group Tier 2 weight management services and Structured Support Group Tier 2 weight management services with Integrated Physical Activity Sessions. These will form lots 1 and 2 of the Framework Agreement.
      
      This Light Touch Regime Framework Agreement has been let under Regulations 74 to 77 of the Public Contract Regulations 2015 (Light Touch Regime), under which the Council has flexibility as to the process or procedure to be used when purchasing certain services, of which health services is one. In this instance, the Council is establishing a Framework Agreement with multiple suppliers that will set out the terms and conditions for making specific purchases (call-offs). The Framework Agreement differs from those let under the non-Light Touch Regime in that the Council, exercising its flexibility, may periodically open the framework for new applicants and may periodically add new lots to the framework agreement that are relevant to the scope of the framework agreement.
      
      It is the Council's intention that new providers will be able to join at certain intervals. It is the Council's intention that the Light Touch Regime Framework will be open for further applications at least once per year for the life of the framework. The Council reserves the right, however, not to open the framework for new applications if it deems this appropriate. If the Council decides to open the Light Touch Regime Framework to new applicants, it will do so on the same terms and conditions and on the same criteria as stated in the original Invitation to Tender, unless the Council deems that amendments are required as a result of changes in the market or changes within the Council.

Through this commissioning process we will commission and evaluate online media literacy intervention pilots in order to develop this evidence base and to share good practice within the sector. An expectation of commissioned organisations is that aspects of your evaluation and learning will be shared widely. 

We know that online media literacy levels are uneven across the UK and that some communities are significantly underserved by current interventions. The focus of this commission is older adults and/or people at risk of digital exclusion. We are looking for targeted, local interventions that help to develop the online safety of people in these communities. This is might include one or more of the following, but is not limited to:
-	Developing resilience to online scams and fraud
-	Building skills around online consumer behaviours e.g. finding the best energy deals
-	Improved awareness of misinformation and disinformation

In February 2025, the Government wrote to all council leaders in areas with two-tier structures, asking them to put forward proposals for local government reorganisation.       The Council have appointed a consultant to provide transition support for Local Government Reorganisation in Norfolk following the Government's minded-to decision. title: CMF 042 Stonebridge - Wretham Peddars Way
description:
Request for quotes sent to three suppliers on 30 September.
Deadline for submission of quotes 30 October 2021.

Reason for works:
	This section of the Peddars way has fallen into disrepair following extensive flooding during the winter of 2020/2021

Following this flooding the path has suffered from increasing amounts of damage due to very soft surface.

Description of works:
	Surface scrape  up to 100mm to 3 metre width x 600 metres length to create level surface 

Surface to be laid as highlighted in attached drawings (Type 1 sub-base with granite fines mechanically tamped down)

Also running on the right hand side (bridge side) a Culvert needs to be installed to take away any surface runoff caused by the slope of the path into the soakaway. This needs to be approx. 9m long and 1.5 metres deep and filled with pea shingle to allow water to soak into the drain.

New surface laid throughout the 600 metres with a cross camber to allow any surface water to drain into the French drain and aqua cell area

Assumed items:	•	Four 1000mm x 500mm x 400mm Aquacell CORE-R units. 
•	9m X 1.5M X 1M Stone filled soakaway
•	3 metre x 600 metre surface scrape 
•	Installation of new improved surface (Type 1 sub-base with granite fines mechanically tamped down)


Delivered Outputs/Outcomes 	1.	600m (x 3 metres) Improved surface for all users of the Peddars way

2.	Improved drainage on the route

3.	Vegetation clearance and crest lifting to allow more light and air into area

title: Provision of Social Prescribing Digital Solution to Support NHS Norfolk and Waveney Integrated Care Board (ICB)
description:
Norfolk and Waveney Integrated care Board utilised the Health Systems Support Framework (HSSF) to procure a social prescribing digital platform to support resilience and maturity of social prescribing offers, whilst providing improvements to care for our community.  

The requirement emphasises the need for seamless integration, secure data handling, and continuous improvement to enhance personalised care and support for the community.

Personalised Care and social prescribing form part of a targeted initiative by NHS England to address health inequalities by focusing on wider determinants such as debt, housing, isolation, and physical inactivity. Evidence has shown socio-economic factors, influencing health and well-being by 40%, outweighing other contributors like health behaviours (30%), clinical care (20%), and the built environment (10%).

Moreover, integrating social prescribing with existing services in Norfolk and Waveney, aims to provide a centralised access point for digital devices, data, and support. This approach enhances reporting mechanisms, identifies gaps, and ensures inclusivity, particularly for those with protected characteristics or belonging to inclusion health groups, especially for patients at risk of digital exclusion.

This service aligns with the Shared Care Record, establishing a Social Prescribing Digital Platform to facilitate seamless referrals to non-clinical provisions. The platform serves as a case management system for non-clinical activities and offers an overview of input and output. The goal is to streamline access to care, support proactive personalised care through integrated teams, and contribute to health equity.

Further backed by two key recommendations for the health and care system: 

The publication of the Fuller Report: Next Steps for Integrating Primary Care (2022) gives a clear mandate for the contribution of non-clinical services in achieving the objectives of: 
•	Streamlining access to care and advice 
•	Providing more proactive, personalised care supported through a neighbourhood Integrated Team
•	Helping people to stay well for longer.

The publication of the Hewitt review provides recommendations to support health equity and improvement though: 
•	Empowering patients through the NHS app and new Citizen Health Accounts
•	Embed health promotion at all levels to improve population health and ensure the longer-term sustainability of the health and care system.

The expansion of virtual ward capacity is a key component in the Norfolk & Waveney system plans to address UEC pressures whilst at the same time improving the patient experience and care.

The procurement, for the provision of hardware, software and associated services (logistics, data and infection control cleansing) has been made via the Spark DPS platform for an initial two year term with the option to extend by a further one year period - to establish the new service offering.

title: Nitrogen and Phosphorous Mitigation Agreement
description:
Norfolk Environmental Credits Limited ('the Purchaser') is a collaboration between Breckland Council, Broadland District Council, North Norfolk Council and South Norfolk Council. 
In securing the services for the generation, establishment and sale of nutrient mitigation credits, the Purchaser has entered into an agreement with the supplier for the allocation of the nutrient pollution savings (Phosphorus and Nitrogen benefit measured in kg/yr) for the purposes of generating nutrient credits. The supplier provides high efficiency (HE) nutrient removal package treatment plants (PTP) for the generation, establishment and sale of nutrient mitigation credits. The services include the calculation of the nutrient benefit in accordance with a robust scientific evidence base and securing the nutrient benefit for a minimum period of 90 years. 
The Purchaser has undertaken market analysis in the design of the services. A call for nutrient offset investment opportunities has been published on the Purchaser's website and soft market engagement has been undertaken with those service providers who have approached the Purchaser. The Purchaser had a specific requirement to identify a supplier who could generate nutrient benefit through upgrading existing septic tanks to high efficiency nutrient removal package treatment plants. At the time of contract award the appointed supplier are the only company which has demonstrated it is able to provide a tradable nutrient benefit (Phosphorus and Nitrogen measured in kg/yr) in the geographical catchment area of the European protected sites as required by the legal framework and in which the Purchaser is seeking to secure the nutrient mitigation.
Accordingly, after due consideration, the Purchaser has decided to make a direct award pursuant to Regulation 32(2)(b)(ii) of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 on the grounds that competition is absent for technical reasons.

title: Prison Education Service Core Education Lot 2: Bedfordshire, Cambridgeshire and Norfolk Group and Hertfordshire, Essex and Suffolk Group
description:
This notice is for the award of Lot 2: Bedfordshire, Cambridgeshire and Norfolk Group and Hertfordshire, Essex and Suffolk Group

The Prisoner Education Services (PES) is a UK government initiative with three overarching strategic priorities; improving prisoner numeracy and literacy skills, incentivizing prisoners to improve their qualifications and skills to increase their prospects of finding work on release, and ensuring that Governors and their teams have the knowledge, tools, support and accountabilities that they need to make this work. PES seeks to transform learning in jails as part of a renewed push to skill up offenders and protect the public.   

PES Core Education will include teaching and delivery of a two-layered curriculum for independence and for opportunity which meets the needs of prisoners, as well as high quality, timely screening and assessment delivery and tailored and impactful additional learning needs support.  
 
The Ministry of Justice launched the PES Panel to reform how education is delivered across the adult prison estate in England. The first call-offs under this framework focused on Core Education Services, including teaching and delivery of a two-layered curriculum for independence (essential subjects such as English, Maths, digital skills) and curriculum for opportunity, which meets the needs of prisoners. The Core Education contracts also include high quality, timely screening and assessment delivery; tailored and impactful additional learning needs support; and (where applicable) prison library services. The contracts are split into 11 regional lots and aim to provide a consistent, high-quality education offer that supports rehabilitation, reduces reoffending, and improves employability and resettlement outcomes for prisoners. 
 
The procurement was conducted under the Open Procedure in accordance with the Light Touch Regime of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015.
